title: HALRO 2.3 display miniature, 1:48, on a 40 mm round base
subject: Civilian twin-boom pusher mapping UAS (published top-level numbers only: 3.6 m span, ~1 m pod, 22 mm booms 0.9 m apart, raised inverted-V tail, 18 in pusher). No internal layout, electronics or mass data.
frame: x aft from the nose, y to port, z up; model millimetres after scaling

wing.note: span station s, leading-edge x, chord

gimbal.note: stylised belly camera ball, position not from the source design

heroic.why: miniature_scale_convert flags wing tip (0.50 mm), tail (0.42 mm), booms (0.46 mm wire, 22.7 mm long) and prop blades (0.25 mm) below the MSLA limits; these are thickened to read at arm's length and survive washing. Planform, span and stations stay true to scale.

base.vent_why: printed flat on the plate, the magnet pocket is sealed by the plate (a suction cup in miniature_printability_check); the vent groove lets resin in and out

stand.why: rod wider than both pegs so each joint seats on a shoulder

upper_joint.pad_why: first check found 0.16-0.38 mm walls between the socket and the curved belly; a 4 mm mount pad gives 0.9 mm

kit.joints_from: miniature_base_and_peg (resin, glue fit, 0.1 mm per side); check.py re-asks the tool and fails if these drift
